question:
A start-up models the number of app users over time $t$ (months) as $N(t) = 5000 \cdot (1 - e^{-0.2t})$.

(a) Find the rate of user increase at $t$ months.

(b) At what time is the rate of user increase fastest?

(c) Confirm with the sign of second derivative.
explanation:
(a) $N'(t) = 5000\cdot 0.2 e^{-0.2t} = 1000 e^{-0.2t}$

(b) Rate is largest when $e^{-0.2t}$ is largest, i.e., $t=0$.

So fastest rate of increase is at $t=0$.

(c) $N''(t) = -200 e^{-0.2t}<0$ always.

So the rate decreases, confirming the fastest at $t=0$.

options.A:
(a) $N'(t)=1000e^{-0.2t}$
(b) The rate of user increase is fastest at $t=0$.
(c) $N''(t)=-200e^{-0.2t}<0$, so the rate decreases with time.
options.B:
(a) $N'(t)=5000e^{-0.2t}$
(b) The rate of user increase is fastest at $t=5$.
(c) $N''(t)>0$, so the rate increases with time.
options.C:
(a) $N'(t)=1000e^{0.2t}$
(b) The rate of user increase is fastest as $t$ becomes large.
(c) $N''(t)=200e^{0.2t}>0$, so the rate increases with time.
options.D:
(a) $N'(t)=200e^{-0.2t}$
(b) The rate of user increase is fastest at $t=10$.
(c) $N''(t)=0$, so the rate is constant.
